heroTitle: From Land Assembly to Integrated Operations
heroDescription: Nord's evolution from acquiring abandoned properties to operating the district's only processor demonstrates systematic execution. Each acquisition and discovery built toward today's dual-track strategy.
historyDescription: When others abandoned the Cobalt camp during low silver prices, Nord quietly assembled the district's largest land package.
historyList1Description: Acquired Castle Mine, Beaver, and Violet properties through share exchange. Secured 11 levels of underground workings, three shafts, and extensive historical data.
historyList2Description: Grew land position from initial 28 km² to 78 km² through staking and strategic acquisitions. Connected Castle Mine to high-potential eastern areas.
historyList3Description: Established formal partnerships with Matachewan, Temagami, and Teme-Augama Anishnabai before exploration began.
temiskamingTitle: TTL: From Government Lab to Production Hub
temiskamingDescription: Acquired the former Ontario government assay lab for a fraction of replacement cost. This 20,000 sq ft facility had served the district since 1941, processing millions of ounces for Agnico and Teck. Nord invested in crushing circuits (20 tonne/hour), gravity plant (24 tonne/day), and analytical capabilities (6,000 assays/month).
batteryDescription: First major discovery in the camp in 50 years. Drilling intersected 89,853 g/t silver, defining an initial 7.5M oz resource. Ongoing 60,000m program targeting 30-100M oz. Multiple vein structures identified including Robinson, Big Silver, and All-Stars zones.
batteryList3: Open for expansion in all directions
goldDescription: Advancing on multiple fronts: MICA funding for Re-2Ox pilot, recovery permits under Ontario's 80-day process, Miller Creek tailings testing (up to 411 g/t AgEq), and continued resource expansion drilling.
denisDescription: While Nord holds battery metals properties in Quebec and lithium claims in Ontario, the company's focus remains on maximizing value from the Castle-TTL complex. This concentration of effort distinguishes Nord from juniors spreading resources across multiple projects.
